lead: Grand Prairie plumbing deals with clay soil, slab foundations and homes from the 1950s to today. PipeMend sends licensed local plumbers across Grand Prairie.
risk: slab leaks from shifting clay, cast-iron drains in older homes and burst pipes in freezes
risk_short: slab leaks, old drains and frozen pipes
why: Older parts of Grand Prairie, near Downtown and Dalworth, have homes from the 1950s to the 1970s with cast-iron drains and aging copper under the slab. Lake Ridge and Mira Lagos were built mostly after 2000.
The ground here is expansive clay that swells after rain and shrinks in drought, bending lines under slabs. Rare hard freezes burst attic and exterior-wall pipes.
water: Grand Prairie buys treated water from Dallas, Fort Worth and Arlington and also uses wells. It is moderately hard.
tips: Water your foundation evenly in dry summers.
Scope cast-iron drains in older homes.
Know where your main shutoff is.
areas: PipeMend works in Downtown Grand Prairie, Westchester, Lake Ridge, Mira Lagos, Dalworth, the Peninsula and every other Grand Prairie neighborhood.
permits: Plumbing permits come from the City of Grand Prairie Building Inspections Division, and plumbers must hold a Texas license.

faq.q: Where does Grand Prairie get its water?
faq.a: Grand Prairie buys treated water from Dallas, Fort Worth and Arlington and adds some well water. The blend is moderately hard.
